The debt: four months for a boat. The holder: the estate and its steward Hulm-Tei. The terms: her food, the boat's upkeep and sick days are added to it. The exit in law: worked off. The exit in practice: bought out, or gone. What she wants: to go home to her tree.
Bought down, she owes nothing but the estate keeps her boat; slipped away, she can never go back to the swamp road, and the estate men are rougher with the next one held.
none: the Owing runs on; the channel is taken at night.
Her grey first (k3), then the steward's true account (k1), then the book itself (k2).

The debt: Keeps-The-Old-Count's Owing as the heirs reckon it; Says-It-Plain held for words; Hides-In-Reeds for a killing. The holder: the heirs of the Rose. The exit in law: none they own to. The exit in practice: the fire. What each wants: out.
Two of the three die in the smoke whichever the player chooses; the one brought out is in the Chainbreakers' keeping and cannot go back to the heirs.
the smoke: a line, not a timer; the way shuts only when the first is out.

The debt: the crew's last season of hire, owed for the Owings he bought. The holder: Ussa-Rekh. The terms: he hires them out until it is worked. The exit in law: the season's end. The exit in practice: breaking the tokens before him. What they want: done a season early.
With the crew, they lose his hire and must find their own on the dock; with him, they work the season and lose their trade on the dock afterwards.
none: the season runs on.

The roll burns: nobody can prove what anyone owes; the gang scatters on the shore. Three places within a day change: the camp (the cutting withdrawn, the clutch grey), the barge (the crew parent off), the paddies behind the camp (the families on the shore).

The Owing roll (labour-and-bondage §2): the debt is months owed, with months added for food; the holder is a Lilmoth debt-labour broker who bought the gang's months from earlier holders (drift 2, transferable) and hires it to Hereguard Plantation; the overseer reads the roll; the exit in law is working the months off, and in practice the food months outrun the work, so the gang families are born into it. The bound want to be home under their own Hist, and have the right to refuse help: the washed-out woman will not leave the gang while her daughter owes.
none the player can stop: the cell cuts the roots at dusk as the player is at the fire; the player can only choose which one of the two witnesses lives

Two of the gang are visibly washed out from years away from their Hist, and their cutting is cut; the player's own line is blank, so no amount of work can pay it down. Whoever the player does not reach in the burning camp dies, and the gang families lose their clutch.
